mission: Integrate Hepta contracts with the sole Codex thread, turn, model and tool execution spine.
runtimeTopology: The existing App Server and Codex Core remain the single thread/turn/model/tool spine. Hepta adapters validate exact context, deadline, payload and observation bindings without creating a second execution engine.
physicalState: Thread store and turn/session state are owned by App Server/Core. External effects stay in operation/effect ledgers. Context and provider payloads are referenced by bounded digests rather than copied into general evidence.
linearization: Thread and turn admission linearize in protocol handlers. Context delivery is recorded only after exact admission. Tool dispatch rechecks final payload and authority at the physical boundary.
recovery: Provider acknowledgement loss and tool timeout remain indeterminate. Recovery preserves thread/turn/operation identities and does not create an ambient model or tool default.
security: Unknown model/session/schema generations reject. Model prose is untrusted data. Tool authority is final-payload-, destination-, epoch- and revocation-bound.
capacity: Context/token limits derive from the selected model profile; tool candidates <=128; queue, first-token, last-token and terminal-tool latency are measured separately.
terminalObserver: App Server/Core observe local admission and streaming state. Provider and tool adapters remain the trusted terminal observers for their own external effects.
externalEvidenceGaps: real model/provider stream identity and terminal observation
deployed Agentd-to-App-Server trace and external tool terminality
